requirements.requirement: The execution checkout is anchored, dirty-state-safe, and compared with the prepared commit before edits.
requirements.acceptance: Anchor report records branch, HEAD, merge-base/delta, SDK, OS, architecture, and preserved working-tree changes.

requirements.requirement: Every platform-sensitive source/project is inventoried and classified by path, filesystem, secret, process, desktop, hosting, test, or external-dependency concern.
requirements.acceptance: Generated inventory covers all projects and has no unclassified P0/P1 item at gate C0.

requirements.requirement: Every persisted path/key/secret record and migration boundary affected by portability is mapped before schema or provider changes.
requirements.acceptance: Persistence map identifies writer, reader, format, migration owner, rollback, and host affinity.

requirements.requirement: Existing stable Windows behavior and available Linux/macOS baselines are captured before implementation.
requirements.acceptance: Baseline evidence includes exact commands, exit codes, logs, and known pre-existing failures.

requirements.requirement: Persisted logical workspace/storage/artifact paths use '/' as their canonical serialized separator.
requirements.acceptance: New writers emit only canonical logical paths; round-trip tests pass on all target OSes.

requirements.requirement: Known legacy logical-path fields accept Windows backslashes on read without treating every Unix backslash as a separator.
requirements.acceptance: Compatibility is field-scoped, versioned, tested, and does not rewrite arbitrary physical paths or filenames.

requirements.requirement: Logical paths, physical host paths, routes/URIs, executable identifiers, and opaque command/script text have distinct contracts.
requirements.acceptance: Inventory and APIs prevent a normalization routine from crossing categories.

requirements.requirement: Portable configuration roots support '~' and an explicit environment-token syntax, while legacy Windows tokens remain readable where required.
requirements.acceptance: Windows, Linux, and macOS tests cover expansion, unset variables, escaping, and fail-safe diagnostics.

requirements.requirement: Foreign absolute path syntax is never silently reinterpreted as a relative path on another OS.
requirements.acceptance: Windows drive/UNC and Unix absolute paths are detected, marked host-bound/unresolved, and require explicit rebind or migration.

requirements.requirement: Infrastructure, storage, MAF workspace, and MAF runtime containment share compatible semantics without creating reverse project references.
requirements.acceptance: Contract tests feed identical logical/physical cases through each owner and prove equivalent outcomes.

requirements.requirement: External-root aliases use a versioned platform-neutral format.
requirements.acceptance: Aliases round-trip Unix roots, Windows roots, and multiple allowed roots without exposing physical paths to untrusted output.

requirements.requirement: Traversal, rooted input, dot segments, empty segments, and invalid logical names fail consistently.
requirements.acceptance: Named negative tests cover '/', '\', '..', drive roots, UNC, symlink candidates, and Unicode edge cases.

requirements.requirement: All persisted logical path writers are deterministic and independent of host separators.
requirements.acceptance: Golden serialization fixtures are byte-equivalent across Windows, Linux, and macOS.

requirements.requirement: Path conversion is localized to typed boundaries rather than a repository-wide string replacement.
requirements.acceptance: Architecture scan shows no blanket slash rewrite in URLs, project files, scripts, or opaque command content.

requirements.requirement: Logical identifiers use ordinal semantics; physical path equality uses a root/volume-specific filesystem policy.
requirements.acceptance: Case-sensitive and case-insensitive volume fixtures or actual-host probes are covered, including macOS uncertainty.

requirements.requirement: All decision-bearing or persisted filesystem enumeration is explicitly sorted by normalized logical key.
requirements.acceptance: Determinism tests randomize source enumeration and assert identical results.

requirements.requirement: Managed roots and trusted operations have one documented symlink/reparse policy applied to reads, writes, opens, process targets, and migrations.
requirements.acceptance: Linux symlink and Windows reparse/junction tests prove containment; unsupported ambiguous cases fail closed.

requirements.requirement: Path checks and file operations minimize time-of-check/time-of-use gaps and document residual platform limits.
requirements.acceptance: Security review accepts the implementation and failure cases cannot escape a managed root in test fixtures.

requirements.requirement: Catalog, storage, control-plane, key, and vault writes use a shared atomic same-volume commit pattern where applicable.
requirements.acceptance: Crash/failure injection leaves either the previous complete generation or the new complete generation, never truncation.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent application processes coordinate writes with bounded cross-process locking or a transactional authority.
requirements.acceptance: Two-process contention tests prove timeout, recovery, and no corruption.

requirements.requirement: Secret-bearing directories and files receive restrictive Unix modes and are verified after creation/migration.
requirements.acceptance: Linux/macOS tests verify expected modes; hardening failure blocks secret use with actionable diagnostics.

requirements.requirement: Physical artifact filenames follow an application-level portable policy independent of Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars.
requirements.acceptance: Golden cases produce the same physical name on all OSes while preserving original display names.

requirements.requirement: File watchers are treated as hints and recover through deterministic rescan/fingerprint or polling.
requirements.acceptance: Overflow, duplicate, rename, and dropped-event tests converge to correct state.

requirements.requirement: Temporary files, locks, and migration markers are cleaned safely without following links or deleting outside owned roots.
requirements.acceptance: Failure-injection and malicious-link fixtures prove bounded cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Windows, Linux, and macOS have explicit default roots for workspace, control-plane data, keys, logs/state, and temporary runtime artifacts.
requirements.acceptance: Root matrix is documented and actual-host tests confirm writable, owned, non-repository locations.

requirements.requirement: Interactive-user and service/headless profiles can override roots without changing persisted logical locators.
requirements.acceptance: systemd/launchd/service-user scenarios use explicit configuration and retain identical application semantics.

requirements.requirement: Storage locators and related JSON/database records are versioned and migrate legacy separator formats transactionally.
requirements.acceptance: Migration can dry-run, back up, resume, roll back, and produce a redacted report.

requirements.requirement: Absolute workspace roots, storage roots, repository paths, and executable preferences are explicitly host-bound.
requirements.acceptance: Foreign records become unresolved with a safe UX/API status rather than being executed or opened.

requirements.requirement: Database profile control-plane records preserve password decryptability while workspace roots are migrated/rebound.
requirements.acceptance: Profile selection, restart, old-data read, and rollback tests pass.

requirements.requirement: Preferred application records are versioned by platform/host and never auto-launch a foreign executable path.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-host import requires explicit confirmation/rebind and desktop launch remains disabled by default.

requirements.requirement: FileSystemStorageDriver Save/Replace semantics are atomic, conflict-aware, and consistent across processes.
requirements.acceptance: Concurrent writes, revision conflicts, cancellation, and crash simulation pass on Windows/Linux/macOS.

requirements.requirement: Storage bootstrap authority compares canonical roots using the owning filesystem semantics and migration state.
requirements.acceptance: Copied or rebound profiles select the intended authoritative storage and reject ambiguous duplicates.

requirements.requirement: A pre-migration backup and rollback path exists for control-plane files, storage catalog records, and path-bearing database data.
requirements.acceptance: Operator rehearsal restores the previous application version and data without loss.

requirements.requirement: Auto secret-provider selection never returns an unsupported provider.
requirements.acceptance: Startup either registers a proven provider or fails fast with a non-secret remediation message.

requirements.requirement: The macOS interactive profile has a real Keychain-backed secret implementation or an explicitly supported secure alternative.
requirements.acceptance: Native contracts prove create/read/update/delete/restart/concurrency/access-control behavior now; genuine macOS execution is tracked as non-blocking follow-up MACOS-KEYCHAIN-VALIDATION-001, and support remains actual-host unverified until it passes.
requirements.status: Implemented — actual macOS validation explicitly deferred; Gate C2 GO

requirements.requirement: The Linux interactive profile has a real Secret Service implementation with explicit session/availability semantics.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover available service, locked/unavailable service, and headless absence; no silent fallback occurs.

requirements.requirement: Linux/macOS headless operation has an explicit secure provider that does not depend on an interactive keyring.
requirements.acceptance: A configured certificate, remote vault, or externally supplied wrapping-key mode is documented and restart-tested.

requirements.requirement: The Data Protection key ring is protected at rest in supported production profiles.
requirements.acceptance: The selected protector is bootstrapped independently, restart-tested, and its files/keys meet permission policy.

requirements.requirement: Key-ring protection has no circular dependency on secrets encrypted by that same key ring.
requirements.acceptance: Architecture test/review traces bootstrap dependencies and detects cycles.

requirements.requirement: The legacy DataProtectionFile provider remains Development/migration-only; Unix may use its encrypted file format only through the explicitly named and honestly classified LocalUserFile basic tier.
requirements.acceptance: Windows Auto selects DPAPI; Unix Auto selects LocalUserFile with 0700 directories, 0600 files, a typed BasicLocal capability, and a same-user threat-model warning; explicit strong providers fail closed and the legacy provider name is rejected in production.

requirements.requirement: Legacy DPAPI-protected data has a Windows-side transactional export/re-encryption path before Unix migration.
requirements.acceptance: Dry-run, interruption, retry, verification, and rollback preserve every source record.

requirements.requirement: Legacy Data Protection secret records and control-plane database passwords remain readable through migration and restart.
requirements.acceptance: Golden fixtures from the old key ring decrypt before and after staged migration.

requirements.requirement: Vault payloads and key metadata are versioned, atomic, cross-process safe, permission-hardened, and rotatable.
requirements.acceptance: Rotation interruption/recovery tests prove no key/payload orphaning and old generation retention until commit.

requirements.requirement: Secret values never enter logs, exceptions, receipts, migration reports, scanner output, or test artifacts.
requirements.acceptance: Automated redaction tests and artifact scan pass with seeded sentinel secrets.

requirements.requirement: Provider capability and health diagnostics reveal only provider type/state and remediation, never identifiers or values.
requirements.acceptance: Readiness/UI/API snapshots are security-reviewed.

requirements.requirement: Secret migration and deletion are auditable without exposing values and have explicit orphan cleanup semantics.
requirements.acceptance: Staged reference cleanup and old-payload deletion are idempotent and tested.

requirements.requirement: A local installation can start without an interactive or externally managed vault by using an honestly classified basic local provider.
requirements.acceptance: Windows startup/restart uses DPAPI with typed Strong protection; Unix startup/restart uses LocalUserFile with enforced 0700/0600 modes, typed BasicLocal protection, and a same-user warning; explicit strong-provider selection, legacy Development compatibility, and non-disclosure remain proven.

requirements.requirement: Portability uses narrow purpose-owned ports/adapters rather than a broad IPlatformService or scattered feature branches.
requirements.acceptance: Dependency and code scan show OS checks only in composition, root resolvers, and leaf native adapters unless justified.

requirements.requirement: Composition selects exactly one implementation for mandatory path/secret primitives and truthful zero-or-one implementations for optional desktop/runtime capabilities.
requirements.acceptance: Startup tests cover every target profile and missing-dependency path.

requirements.requirement: Capability descriptors include availability, reason, remediation, execution boundary, and tested support level.
requirements.acceptance: Workbench/settings/readiness surfaces consume descriptors without inferring support from OS name alone.

requirements.requirement: External package and native-service capabilities can be quarantined independently without blocking headless core startup.
requirements.acceptance: FileTools, Secret Service, Keychain, terminal, and process-discovery failures degrade only their declared optional capabilities.

requirements.requirement: Current MAF/process ownership boundaries remain intact after platform composition changes.
requirements.acceptance: Architecture tests preserve no reverse MAF-to-product/process semantic dependency.

requirements.requirement: The Web host starts headlessly on Windows and Ubuntu with desktop launch disabled; macOS publish/service contracts remain explicitly unverified until A07 actual-host execution.
requirements.acceptance: Bounded Windows/Ubuntu startup, health, restart, rollback, and shutdown smoke tests pass from clean publish output; macOS is labeled ActualHostUnverified and tracked as A07-MACOS-HEADLESS-ACTUALHOST-001.

requirements.requirement: Framework-dependent publish is proven for win-x64, linux-x64, osx-x64, and osx-arm64; additional RIDs are claims only after proof.
requirements.acceptance: Artifacts run outside the repository and include a support manifest.

requirements.requirement: Linux systemd and macOS launchd runbooks define service user, roots, environment, restart, logs, permissions, upgrade, and rollback.
requirements.acceptance: Runbooks are rehearsed or clearly mark unexecuted optional desktop steps.

requirements.requirement: Installation logic separates cross-platform publish/configuration from Windows shortcuts and Unix service integration.
requirements.acceptance: The existing PowerShell installer remains valid while Unix entry points do not duplicate security/path policy.

requirements.requirement: Operational diagnostics report platform, configured roots, provider/capability state, and support profile without exposing secrets or unnecessary absolute paths.
requirements.acceptance: Redacted diagnostic bundle is validated on each target OS.

requirements.requirement: Developer and operator documentation no longer presents %LOCALAPPDATA%, PowerShell, or Windows desktop behavior as universal.
requirements.acceptance: Documentation includes Linux/macOS prerequisites, limitations, migrations, and explicit unsupported features.

requirements.requirement: An active GitHub Actions workflow restores, builds, and runs the stable test gate on Windows, Ubuntu, and macOS.
requirements.acceptance: All three jobs are required checks or otherwise protected by repository policy evidence.
requirements.status: Implemented — exact-commit hosted checks and repository policy evidence pending

requirements.requirement: Actual-host tests cover path, filesystem, storage, secret-provider selection, permissions, and headless startup.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cannot pass solely through a mocked OS enum.
requirements.status: Implemented — Windows/Ubuntu pass; genuine macOS pending hosted CI

requirements.requirement: Linux and macOS restart tests prove protected state, storage catalogs, and migrated records remain readable.
requirements.acceptance: At least one old-format fixture and one new-format fixture survive restart on each supported migration route.
requirements.status: Implemented — Ubuntu restart passes; genuine macOS pending hosted CI

requirements.requirement: Publish artifacts and service/headless smoke tests run from clean directories outside the repository.
requirements.acceptance: No success depends on bin/obj, developer profile, global npm cache, or repository-relative mutable state.
requirements.status: Implemented — Windows/Ubuntu pass; genuine macOS pending hosted CI

requirements.requirement: Windows stable behavior remains green after every core portability phase.
requirements.acceptance: No compatibility change is accepted with unexplained Windows regression.
requirements.status: Satisfied locally — exact-commit hosted Windows confirmation pending

requirements.requirement: Static scanning blocks new unowned OS checks, raw Windows-only tokens, unsafe absolute-path persistence, and insecure secret fallbacks.
requirements.acceptance: Allowlist entries are narrow, reviewed, and source-linked.
requirements.status: Implemented and locally enforced — hosted static check pending

requirements.requirement: Core Gate C4 produces a versioned handoff anchor and evidence pack that is sufficient to start the runtime bundle.
requirements.acceptance: Runtime bundle remains blocked until C4 is GO and its source references are refreshed.
requirements.status: Blocked — C4 requires an exact pushed commit and hosted evidence
